content.title: US holiday sales set for slowest growth since pandemic, Deloitte report forecasts
content.summary: -U.S. holiday sales are projected to grow at their slowest pace since the pandemic, Deloitte said in a forecast released on Wednesday, as macroeconomic uncertainties weigh on consumer spending.  Holiday shopping is a critical sales driver for retailers, especially amid uncertain demand and persistent inflation, compounded by the lingering effects of U.S. President Donald Trump's volatile trade policies.  Retailers, in recent weeks, have issued mixed forecasts heading into the holiday season.

content.title: Helped by brand tie-ups, Lego's first-half sales hit a record
content.description:
STORY: Lego's first-half sales hit a new record.

The Danish toymaker announced Wednesday sales rose 12% during the period to $5.43 billion.

Partnerships with other major brands like Formula One and Jurassic Park helped it outperform rivals.

Operating profit for the first six months was also up by a tenth to almost $425 million.

CEO Niels Christiansen said, "The toy market is actually back to growth this year, but we are outpacing it and taking market share."

Lego reported growth across all its markets, including China, where it has faced challenges in recent years.

U.S. sales also grew at double-digit rates.

Christiansen said Lego hadn't seen a significant trend for U.S. customers to trade down to cheaper products - despite economic uncertainties related to trade tensions.

He added the company had managed tariff impacts.

Lego's peers, including Hasbro and Barbie-maker Mattel, are more exposed to tariff volatility due to their reliance on Chinese manufacturing.
